status: design, 2026-09-25. No tool reads this file yet: the ruin transform it describes is not written, so tools/place_town.py still builds the Scar without houses. The towers, terrace walls and the cairn plinth are authored earthworks in data/placements.json (scar_towers, scar_walls, scar_cairn_plinth) and are built today.
note: A ruin is a donor house placed from a ruined copy of its template, the way a re-materialed house is placed from a re-materialed copy (tools/place_town.py rewrite_template, data/rematerial.json house_sets). This file is the authored half: which design stands on which lot, how far each has fallen, and the rules the copy is made by. The generator translates it; it decides nothing. Positions here are derived from the Displaced City's placement report (derived/towns/displaced_city_placement.json: each design's footprint under its rotation gives its size and its entrance side), not read from the NBT; tools/place_town.py re-derives both from the template and refuses a rotation that does not turn the entrance to the recorded facing.

the_scar.decided: the owner, 2026-09-25: a ruined city, not a living one. The Scar is the footprint the Displaced City left when it was moved underground; its foundations line up with the cavern city's streets. It should read as a big abandoned city on the drawn layout.
the_scar.reading: Thirty-three houses stand in ruin on the drawn lots, every one a design the player can find whole in the Displaced City: the same giant-taiga houses in the spruce and cobble they were built in, where the cavern's copies are in cherry and dark oak. Near the old square they stand to their eaves with the roofs gone; toward the rim they are broken walls and then single courses. Two towers still stand, one fallen full length along the ground, and a stump; broken terrace walls cross the bands between the roads. Snow lies on everything and moss in the lee. No light, no door, no bed, no chest: everything that was the people's went with them.
the_scar.seed_rule: every random draw is seeded by sha256(seed + '/' + ruin id + '/' + step name), so a ruin's copy is byte-identical on every rebuild and the audit's expectation does not move
the_scar.twin_rule: each ruin names the Displaced City house of the same design as its twin. The first 24 Displaced City houses are in the donor's own materials, so a Scar ruin of one of those designs is the same house block for block before it fell; houses 25 to 42 are the cavern's re-materialed repeats (displaced_cherry, displaced_dark), and their Scar twins stay in the original spruce and cobble on purpose: the house as it was before it went down

standing.roof: removed; at most one run of roof beam left per ruin
standing.why: the heart of the city, round the old square: walls to the eaves, open to the sky

shell.why: the middle bands: rooms you can still read, windows gone, a wall or two open

half.why: fallen to the sills: the plan of the house, a door frame, a chimney stub

stump.why: the rim, where the wind has had the longest: one or two courses on the floor

transform.applies_to: a copy of the donor template, written into the build pack (never into kits/), one copy per ruin
transform.template_placed: cobblers:towns/ruined/<namespace>/<path>__<ruin id>, written to build/datapacks/cobblers_towns/data/cobblers/structure/towns/ruined/<namespace>/<path>__<ruin id>.nbt, the path tools/town_audit.py expected_buildings already reads a rewritten copy from
order: replace every jigsaw by its final state inside the copy (place_town must then not setblock jigsaw final states after placing a ruin, or it would put back blocks the decay removed)
cut each column to its decay height
transform.keep: the template's ground layer (the entrance jigsaw's layer, tools/place_town.py template_info grade_layer) and everything below it are never cut or swapped, except the floor swaps listed under overgrowth. The floor is what place_town seats on and what its verify tests at each corner, so the seating, the foundation columns and the corners come out as they do for the whole house.
transform.wall_height: eaves_y is the highest layer whose footprint perimeter ring is at least 60% non-air; the wall height of the ruin is eaves_y - grade_layer. Every layer above eaves_y is the roof and is removed in every class (standing keeps at most one straight run of roof beam, chosen by the seeded draw).
transform.decay_height: per template column: grade_layer + max(1, round(wall_height * f)), f = the class's range sampled by 2D value noise over the template's x and z (lattice every 3 blocks, bilinear, seeded per ruin), so neighbouring columns fall together and a wall steps down rather than toothing. Blocks above a column's decay height are removed.
transform.removed_means: dropped from the copy's block list, never written as air: a dropped cell leaves whatever is in the world (snow, the pad) and is not one of the template's rooms, so tools/town_audit.py does not read rubble or snow there as ground in a room. Air the template stores below the decay height (its rooms) stays.
transform.breaches: per outer wall face, the class's count of gaps 2 to 4 blocks wide, from grade_layer + 1 + (0 to 2) up to the decay height, never on the entrance column and the one each side of it (the doorway stays walkable)

remove_blocks.light_why: nothing lights the Scar (plan.lighting.dark_by_design); a donor house's lanterns are the one thing that would
remove_blocks.spawn_blocks_why: the two blocks a village house or a ruin could carry that data/spawn_blocks.json lists; nothing in data/spawn_block_policy.json allows them at the Scar
remove_blocks.belongings_why: the city went with its people: no container, no bed, no workstation, no door, no glass left in a frame. Removing the containers also removes every donor loot table, so there is nothing at the Scar for players to race each other to

weathering.rule: each surviving block above the ground layer is swapped with the listed chance, else kept; a block with two swaps draws once across both (stone brick: 30% cracked, 15% mossy, 55% kept); a swap to null removes the block
weathering.states: a swap keeps the block's properties (facing, half, shape) where the new block has them

rubble.rule: inside the footprint only, on the first layer above the floor, in air cells within 2 blocks inside a breach or a wall cut by more than 2 courses; the count is 15% of the wall blocks the decay and breaches removed; never in the doorway (entrance column and one each side, three deep)

palette.why: a fallen beam; axis x or z by the draw

rubble.never_why: tools/town_audit.py counts those as ground inside a room (NATURAL_GROUND) and would report the ruin buried

overgrowth.snow: minecraft:snow[layers=1] on 35% and layers=2 on 10% of the top faces the copy leaves open to the sky (floor and wall tops), only on full blocks. Natural snowfall at y280 adds to it; tools/town_audit.py compares block names, so a changed layer count still matches
overgrowth.moss_carpet: on 15% of open floor cells without snow
overgrowth.moss_block: 10% of the open floor's stone and cobble (the one swap allowed in the ground layer; still a full floor block, so the verify's corners hold)
overgrowth.vine: on 12% of the inner faces of the surviving north walls, between the second course and the decay height; only where the vine's cell is inside the template's bounds
overgrowth.not_why: glow lichen gives light (the Scar has none); cobweb decides spawns (data/spawn_blocks.json)

transform.outside_the_footprint: the transform writes nothing outside a ruin's footprint: the lot outlines (scar_foundations) and the streets stay as the plan draws them, and the rubble and walls between the lots are the authored earthworks
transform.spawn_blocks: every block the transform adds (cracked and mossy stone brick and cobble and their stairs, slabs and walls, cobblestone and its slab, stone brick slab, spruce log, snow, moss carpet, moss block, vine, coarse dirt) was checked against data/spawn_blocks.json on 2026-09-25: none is listed. The donor houses already pass the placed-template check for the Displaced City, and the transform only removes and swaps

audit.place_town: a placement with a ruin record is seated exactly as the whole house (template_info from the original file: entrance, grade layer, base columns and corners), then placed from the ruined copy, and records the copy in its report's template_placed; its jigsaw setblocks are skipped (the copy has none); its loot removals are skipped (the copy has no containers)
audit.verify: unchanged: the corners and the columns under the floor are the whole house's, which the transform does not touch
audit.town_audit: expected_buildings reads the copy the report names, so it expects the ruin's blocks, not the whole house's, with no change to its model; STANDING applies as for any building. The only extension needed is for any rubble a later version writes outside a footprint, which this design does not
audit.plan_audit: streets and plaza keep their paving: nothing in this design writes on a planned road cell except scar_cairn_plinth, on the plaza, which the audit exempts as an earthwork. No lamp: the plan's lamp is none

ruins.why: the temple is ten blocks deep and no lot's nine-block interior holds it, so it stands off the lots, on the west side of the avenue near its north end, its door to the road: the tallest house ruin, the last building before the road runs out

the_scar.lot_fit: every footprint is inside its lot's interior (the lot rect less its one-block foundation outline, 10 by 9), set against the road side and centred along it, so scar_foundations (which runs after the templates) never overwrites a ruin and each outline reads as the plinth of the plot the house stood on
the_scar.file_rule: each template's local copy is kits/structures/incoming/townkit/<namespace>/<path>.nbt, gitignored: Repurposed Structures' houses are not redistributable and are placed by id (the Displaced City's donor_source); the ruined copies exist only in build/

earthworks.scar_foundations: one course of stone brick outlining each of the 32 lots (unchanged)
earthworks.scar_towers: tower A standing to y302 with a broken crown, west of the avenue on the north band (2057-2063, 911-917); tower B fallen, its stump at (2178-2182, 912-916) and its shaft in three lengths lying west to x2150; tower C standing roofless to y296 on the south band east of the avenue (2172-2178, 982-988); tower D a stump on the south band west of it (2043-2047, 983-987)
earthworks.scar_walls: two broken terrace walls, z925 and z975, 25 blocks either side of the cross road, x2006 to x2200 with the avenue and plaza left open, one to four courses, with gaps and rubble
earthworks.scar_cairn_plinth: a 5 by 5 ring of chiseled stone brick round an empty 3 by 3 of paving at the centre of the old square: the Displaced City's summit cairn is 3 by 3

avenue_end.intent: the old avenue runs north across the whole disc and stops at the cliff edge, in the air
avenue_end.state: not built. The plan's avenue is paved to z803 on the pad; what lies north of the pad's edge is the press_pads feather (radius 150, feather 140), which may be a slope rather than a drop. Whether there is a cliff to end at is a heightmap question this design cannot answer without reading it
avenue_end.rule_for_the_generator: from the avenue's last planned row northward, at y280 and the avenue's width, carry the deck while tools/ground.py ground under the centre line is below 276, on stone brick piers down to that ground every 6 blocks; stop at the first row where the ground is 12 or more below the deck, or 24 rows past the pad, whichever is first, and break the last 3 rows raggedly (seeded). No railing. If the ground never falls 4 below the deck within 24 rows, build nothing and report that the avenue ends on a slope

the_scar.multiplayer: nothing here is claimed or triggered: no chests, no loot tables, no beds, no respawn point, no one-time event. Several players can walk the ruins at once without contention. The towers are open to the sky and their doorways are 1 wide by 3 high
the_scar.lighting: none, by design (the settlement's plan.lighting.dark_by_design). No ruin keeps a roof over a floor; the towers are open to the sky, and the fallen tower's three lengths (3 by 3 inside, 5 to 8 long) are open at both ends with holes in their sides and tops, so daylight reaches every floor; at night the Scar is as dark as the mountain round it
